method: Crosswalk existing June 2026 CreatorDB primary category channel counts against selected, differently scoped YouTube title events and one US online animation-fan survey. Evaluate denominator, topic definition, observation period and geography before doing arithmetic. All three selected examples fail comparability.

cases.attention_population: Videos uploaded with 'morning routine' or 'morningroutine' in the title (not all lifestyle videos)
cases.reason: Broad vendor People & Blogs primary category is not the same as videos with a morning-routine title predicate; uploads are production events, not audience demand or unique creators.

cases.attention_population: Videos with "drum cover" in the title
cases.reason: Broad vendor Music channel category is not a defined cohort of all video titles with drum cover; half-year video view events are not deduplicated viewers, creator earnings or monthly channel audiences.

cases.attention_population: Online animation fans aged 14–24, n=358, who watch animated series created for YouTube weekly or more
cases.reason: CreatorDB global primary-category channel counts do not share the denominator of an April 2025 US online animation-fan survey aged 14–24. A percentage of 358 surveyed fans is not global audience size.

valid_join_requirements: The same defined category or exact inclusion predicate for creator supply and topic attention
A common observation date or explicitly comparable period for counted active creators and viewing
Same region and visibility frame, with missing-channel selection documented
Audience measured as deduplicated people where a person-to-creator ratio is claimed
Only comparable observed metric units; views, uploads, ad reach and survey percentages cannot convert without a validated bridge
Account for overlapping subcultures and channels posting in multiple topics
Attributable income and production work are independently measured before profitability claims
scope_note: Three selected illustrative incompatibilities from existing sourced research, not a new channel index, census of subcultures, creator-matching exercise or total demand ranking.
